source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, no calculator; part (e) expression for g removed 2026-11-17 for space). Graph of f(x) = 3 sin(2x) - 2 on [0, pi] (solid), max (pi/4, 1), min (3pi/4, -5); dashed g = f translated pi/4 to the left. Version a.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write down the maximum and minimum values of f(x) = a sin(bx) + d from the graph.
parts.notes: A1 for each value. Write down: a bare answer earns the marks.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Write down the period of f.
parts.tolerance: Accept the decimal 3.14 only with a note to give exact values.
parts.notes: Wrong methods, each A0: pi/2 (maximum to minimum is half a period); 2pi (period of sin x).

parts.label: c
parts.notes: M1 for a = (max - min)/2 or d = (max + min)/2, or reading the principal axis y = -2. A1 for a = 3. A1 for d = -2. A1 for b = 2pi/pi = 2. Correct a and d with no working earn M0A1A1; a bare b = 2 earns its A1. Wrong methods: a = 6 (max minus min); swapping a and d (a = -2, d = 3); b = pi or b = 1/2: A0 for that value.
parts.follow_through: FT b from the candidate's period in (b).

parts.label: d
parts.description: State whether g(x) = f(x + pi/4) or g(x) = f(x - pi/4), with a reason.
parts.notes: R1 for a valid reason: the graph of g is the graph of f moved left (e.g. the maximum of f at x = pi/4 is at x = 0 on g), and f(x + h) is a translation to the left; or a check such as g(0) = f(pi/4) = 1. A1 for g(x) = f(x + pi/4). Do not award R0A1: the choice with no reason earns 0. Wrong method: f(x - pi/4) (the sign that matches the direction in words): R0A0.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, no calculator). Unit circle: P at 2pi/3, Q at 315 deg; sin theta = 2/3 in quadrant II. Version a.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Write down the exact coordinates of P (angle 2pi/3).
parts.tolerance: Accept -0.5 for -1/2. The root-3 coordinate must be exact: decimals earn A0 for that coordinate.
parts.notes: A1 for each coordinate with its sign. Wrong method: sine and cosine swapped, (-sqrt3/2, 1/2): A0A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Write 315 degrees in radians as an exact multiple of pi.
parts.tolerance: Accept 315pi/180 unsimplified or a decimal multiple of pi. A decimal with no pi earns A0.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Write down the exact coordinates of Q (angle 315 degrees).
parts.tolerance: Accept 1/sqrt2 for sqrt2/2. Decimals earn A0.
parts.notes: A1 for each coordinate with its sign.

parts.label: e
parts.description: sin theta = 2/3, theta in quadrant II. Use sin^2 + cos^2 = 1 to find cos theta exactly.
parts.notes: M1 for substituting into sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 (squares present). A1 for cos^2 theta = 5/9. A1 for -sqrt5/3 (cosine negative in quadrant II). The final A1 needs the correct sign only: the opposite sign or +/- as the final answer earns M1A1A0. A bare correct answer with no working earns M0A1A1. Wrong method: cos theta = 1 - |sin theta| = 1/3 (squares left out): M0A0A0.

parts.label: f
parts.description: Find the exact value of tan theta.
parts.notes: A1 for sin theta / cos theta with the correct sign.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's cos theta in (e), including its sign.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, calculator, degrees). Quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal AC: AB = 7, BC = 9, angle ABC = 110; angle ACD = 48, angle ADC = 75 (so CAD = 57). Version a.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Find AC (AB = 7, BC = 9, angle ABC = 110 deg).
parts.tolerance: Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for the cosine rule. A1 for the substitution 7^2 + 9^2 - 2(7)(9) cos 110. A1 for 13.2. Wrong methods: sign error gives 9.32: M1A0A0; radian mode gives 16.0: M1A1A0.

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate values; note premature rounding as feedback rather than withholding the accuracy mark. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for the sine rule in triangle ACD. A1 for pairing AD with 48 deg and AC with 75 deg. A1 for 10.1. Wrong method: pairing AD with 75 deg gives 17.1: M1A0A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's AC in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the area of quadrilateral ABCD.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate values; note premature rounding as feedback rather than withholding the accuracy mark. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for a correct area expression for either triangle: (1/2)(7)(9) sin 110, or (1/2)(AC)(AD) sin 57 (angle CAD = 57 may be implied). M1 for adding the two triangle areas. A1 for 85.4. Wrong method: using 110 deg in triangle ACD gives 92.2: M1M1A0. Feedback note on premature rounding if AC or AD was rounded.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's AC and AD.

source: Original (authored 2026-11-17, calculator, radians). Daylight N(t) = a sin(b(t - c)) + d, t days after 31 Dec; NYC max 15.1 (t = 172), min 9.3 (t = 355); Palermo P(t) = p sin(b(t - c)) + q, max 14.8, min 9.5. Version a.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Find a and d from the maximum and minimum.
parts.notes: A1 for a = (max - min)/2 = 2.9; A1 for d = (max + min)/2 = 12.2. Note: bare values earn A1A1 (overrides the bare-answer default). Wrong methods: a = 5.8 (max minus min); a and d swapped: A0 for that value.

parts.label: b
parts.notes: A1. Wrong methods, A0: b = 365; b = 365/(2pi) = 58.1.

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept 81.25 (from the minimum condition) and 3 s.f. forms.
parts.notes: M1 for the maximum condition b(t_max - c) = pi/2, the minimum condition b(t_min - c) = 3pi/2 (or -pi/2), or 'a quarter period before the maximum'. A1 for 80.75. Wrong methods, M0A0: c = 172 (date of the maximum, the cosine shift); c = 355.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Find p and q for the Italian city.
parts.notes: A1 for p = (max - min)/2; A1 for q = (max + min)/2. Bare values earn A1A1.

parts.label: e
parts.description: Today t = 321: how many more minutes of daylight Palermo has than New York.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate values; note premature rounding as feedback rather than withholding the accuracy mark. Examples: 9.50 from c = 81.25; 9.55 from b = 0.0172; 9.6 from 9.93 - 9.77. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for evaluating both models at the given t and subtracting. A1 for 9.57 minutes. Wrong methods: 0.160 (hours, not converted): M1A0; degree mode gives -4.08: M1A0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's a, b, c, d, p, q.

parts.label: f
parts.description: Length of time, in days, during which Palermo has fewer than 10 hours of daylight.
parts.tolerance: Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate values; note premature rounding as feedback rather than withholding the accuracy mark. Example: 72.3 from b = 0.0172. Accept 3 s.f. or the calculator display with an ellipsis; a value cut short with no ellipsis earns A0 (markscheme-spec 21).
parts.notes: M1 for the equation (or a GDC graph with the horizontal line drawn). A1 for both intersection values t = 25.8 (25.7716...) and t = 318 (318.228...). A1 for the length, which wraps around the new year: (365 - later value) + earlier value. Wrong method: later minus earlier = 292 days (the complementary period): M1A1A0. Whole-number answers (e.g. rounding to a whole day) earn the final A0 with a feedback note to give 3 s.f.
